claims.text: What the image looks like BI-RADS (her chart): 0 = incomplete; 1 = negative; 2 = benign; 3 = probably benign (6 mo f/u, <2% malignancy); 4 = suspicious - biopsy (4A low / 4B intermediate / 4C high); 5 = highly suggestive of malignancy (>95%) - biopsy; 6 = known biopsy-proven cancer
claims.quote: 0 = incomplete; 1 = negative; 2 = benign; 3 = probably benign (6 mo f/u, <2% malignancy); 4 = suspicious - biopsy (4A low / 4B intermediate / 4C high); 5 = highly suggestive of malignancy (>95%) - biopsy; 6 = known biopsy-proven cancer

claims.text: Suspicious findings: spiculated mass, pleomorphic clustered microcalcifications, architectural distortion, skin/nipple retraction
claims.quote: Suspicious findings: spiculated mass, pleomorphic clustered microcalcifications, architectural distortion, skin/nipple retraction

claims.text: Density a-d (d = extremely dense → reduced sensitivity)
claims.quote: Density a-d (d = extremely dense → reduced sensitivity)

claims.text: Dense breast tissue seen on screening mammography is associated with an approximately 2-fold increased risk of breast cancer
claims.quote: Dense breast tissue seen on screening mammography is associated with an approximately 2-fold increased risk of breast cancer (14).

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Mammograms are breast radiographs, usually 2 or more views of each breast taken at different angles; the breasts are compressed with plastic paddles to optimize visualization of breast tissue and abnormalities
claims.quote: Mammograms are breast radiographs, which usually include 2 or more views of each breast taken at different angles. The breasts are compressed with plastic paddles to optimize visualization of breast tissue and abnormalities.

claims.text: Screening mammograms check for breast cancer in asymptomatic women; diagnostic mammograms are used in women who have breast symptoms, palpable breast masses, or abnormal screening results that require further investigation
claims.quote: Screening mammograms are used to check for breast cancer in asymptomatic women (see Breast Cancer Screening). Diagnostic mammograms are used to diagnose breast disorders in women who have (1): Breast symptoms Palpable breast masses Abnormal results on screening mammograms that require further investigation

claims.text: Typically about 0.21 mSv of radiation, relatively low compared with other imaging tests that use radiation; radiation exposure is still a concern because breast tissue is sensitive to radiation
claims.quote: Typically, mammography exposes the breasts to about 0.21 mSv of radiation. This dose is relatively low compared with other imaging tests that use radiation (see table ). However, radiation exposure is a concern with mammography because breast tissue is sensitive to radiation (see Risks of Medical Radiation).

claims.text: Tomosynthesis, a 3-dimensional technique, can be used: thin tomographic slices minimize the effect of overlapping structures so abnormalities can be better separated from the background; it may reduce the need for repeat mammograms, and clinicians may be able to detect cancers more accurately, especially in patients with dense breasts
claims.quote: Tomosynthesis, a 3-dimensional technique, can be used in mammography. In tomosynthesis, an x-ray source moves over an arc of excursion, providing thin, tomographic slices, which are reconstructed into 3-dimensional images. This technique minimizes the effect of overlapping structures in the breast. Thus, abnormalities can be better separated from the background. Tomosynthesis may reduce the need for repeat mammograms, and clinicians may be able to detect cancers more accurately, especially in patients with dense breasts.

claims.text: Abnormal screening mammogram → image-guided biopsy; an abnormal breast MRI is typically evaluated with ultrasound to decide whether biopsy should be guided by ultrasound or MRI
claims.quote: For patients with an abnormal screening mammogram, image-guided biopsy is performed. An abnormal breast MRI is typically evaluated with ultrasound to determine whether biopsy should be performed under guidance with ultrasound or MRI.

claims.text: Breast symptoms (eg, pain, nipple discharge) or a palpable mass or other abnormality on clinical breast examination are typically evaluated initially with breast ultrasound; if ultrasound is abnormal or indeterminate, mammography is performed; if imaging suggests cancer, biopsy is performed
claims.quote: Patients who present with breast symptoms (eg, pain, nipple discharge) or a palpable breast mass or other abnormality (eg, skin lesions) on clinical breast examination are typically evaluated initially with breast ultrasound. If ultrasound results are abnormal or indeterminate, mammography is performed. If imaging findings suggest cancer, biopsy is performed.

claims.text: Pearl: breast biopsy should be performed if physical findings (eg, palpable mass) suggest breast cancer, even if mammogram results are negative
claims.quote: Breast biopsy should be performed if physical findings (eg, palpable mass) suggest breast cancer, even if mammogram results are negative.

claims.text: Percutaneous core needle biopsy is preferred to surgical biopsy; stereotactic biopsy (needle biopsy guided by mammography performed in 2 planes) or ultrasound-guided biopsy is commonly used to improve accuracy; clips are placed at the biopsy site so it can be identified with mammography
claims.quote: Percutaneous core needle biopsy is preferred to surgical biopsy. Core biopsy can be performed guided by imaging or palpation (freehand). Stereotactic biopsy (needle biopsy guided by mammography performed in 2 planes and analyzed by computer to produce a 3-dimensional image) or ultrasound-guided biopsy is commonly used to improve accuracy. Clips are placed at the biopsy site so it can be identified with mammography.

claims.text: A positive biopsy specimen should be analyzed for estrogen and progesterone and HER2 receptors; MRI is often used for preoperative planning and can accurately determine tumor size, chest wall involvement and number of tumors
claims.quote: A positive biopsy specimen should be analyzed for estrogen and progesterone and HER2 receptors. MRI is often used by surgeons for preoperative planning; it can accurately determine tumor size, chest wall involvement, and number of tumors.

claims.text: Axillary lymph nodes are the most common site of locoregional spread; the most common sites of distant metastases are bone (51%), liver/soft tissue (19%), pleura (16%), lung (14%) and brain (4%)
claims.quote: While axillary lymph nodes are the most common site of locoregional spread of breast cancer, the most common sites of distant metastases are bone (51% of metastases), liver/soft tissue (19%), pleura (16%), lung (14%), and brain (4%) (3).

claims.text: Common indications for bone scanning: bone pain, elevated serum alkaline phosphatase, stage III or IV cancer
claims.quote: For bone scanning, common indications include the following: Bone pain Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase Stage III or IV cancer

claims.text: Causes Factors that greatly increase risk: breast cancer in close relatives (particularly if a BRCA gene mutation is present), atypical ductal or lobular hyperplasia, lobular carcinoma in situ, and significant exposure to chest radiation therapy before age 30
claims.quote: Factors that greatly increase risk include breast cancer in close relatives (particularly if a BRCA gene mutation is present), atypical ductal or lobular hyperplasia, lobular carcinoma in situ, and significant exposure to chest radiation therapy before age 30.

claims.text: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations increase the risk of developing breast cancer to 70%; prophylactic bilateral mastectomy reduces the risk by 90% and should be offered to women with a BRCA mutation
claims.quote: BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations increase the risk of developing breast cancer to 70% (1). Prophylactic bilateral mastectomy reduces the risk of breast cancer by 90% and should be offered to women with a BRCA mutation.

claims.text: The most common histologic type is epithelial (carcinoma), developing from cells lining breast ducts or lobules; nonepithelial cancers of the supporting stroma are less common
claims.quote: The most common histologic type of breast cancer is epithelial (carcinoma), which develops from cells lining breast ducts or lobules; nonepithelial cancers of the supporting stroma (eg, angiosarcoma, primary stromal sarcomas, phyllodes tumor) are less common.

claims.text: Ductal carcinoma in situ: neoplastic epithelial lesions confined to the breast ducts, with varying histology and malignant potential; usually detected only by mammography
claims.quote: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS): DCIS refers to neoplastic epithelial lesions that are confined to the breast ducts; lesions may have varying histology and malignant potential. It is usually detected only by mammography.

claims.text: Invasive carcinomas are most frequently adenocarcinoma: approximately 75% are infiltrating ductal and 10% of the remaining cases are infiltrating lobular
claims.quote: Invasive carcinomas are most frequently adenocarcinoma. Approximately 75% are infiltrating ductal histology and 10% of the remaining cases are infiltrating lobular carcinomas (5).

claims.text: Mechanism: invades locally and spreads through the regional lymph nodes, bloodstream, or both; metastatic breast cancer may affect almost any organ, most commonly lungs, liver, bone, brain and skin
claims.quote: Breast cancer invades locally and spreads through the regional lymph nodes, bloodstream, or both. Metastatic breast cancer may affect almost any organ in the body—most commonly, lungs, liver, bone, brain, and skin.

claims.text: Symptoms Most breast cancers are detected by mammography; breast pain is the sole presenting symptom in only approximately 1 to 2% of cases; infrequently, the presenting symptom is overall breast enlargement or a nondescript thickening
claims.quote: Most breast cancers are detected by mammography; other modes of detection are self-examination by the patient, clinical breast examination, MRI, and ultrasound (1). Breast pain may be present but is the sole presenting symptom of breast cancer in only approximately 1 to 2% of cases (2). Infrequently, the presenting symptom is overall breast enlargement or a nondescript thickening of the breast.

claims.text: A common examination finding is asymmetry or a dominant mass distinctly different from the surrounding tissue; diffuse fibrotic changes in a quadrant (usually upper outer) are more characteristic of benign disorders; a slightly firmer thickening in one breast but not the other may be a sign of cancer
claims.quote: A common finding during breast examination is asymmetry or a dominant mass—a mass distinctly different from the surrounding breast tissue. Diffuse fibrotic changes in a quadrant of the breast, usually the upper outer quadrant, are more characteristic of benign disorders; a slightly firmer thickening in one breast but not the other may be a sign of cancer.

claims.text: Paget disease of the nipple (underlying in situ or invasive carcinoma): erythema, crusting, scaling and discharge that usually appear so benign the patient might ignore them; approximately 50 to 60% have a palpable mass at presentation
claims.quote: Paget disease of the nipple is associated with an underlying in situ or invasive carcinoma and manifests as skin changes, including erythema, crusting, scaling, and discharge; these changes usually appear so benign that the patient might ignore them, delaying diagnosis. Approximately 50 to 60% of patients with Paget disease of the nipple have a palpable mass at presentation (3).

claims.text: Inflammatory breast cancer: erythema and enlargement of the breast, often without a mass; skin may be discolored or appear thickened, resembling orange peel (peau d’orange)
claims.quote: Inflammatory breast cancer manifests as erythema and enlargement of the breast, often without a mass, and skin may be discolored or appear thickened, resembling orange peel (peau d’orange).

claims.text: More advanced cancers: fixation of the mass to the chest wall or to overlying skin, satellite nodules or ulcers in the skin; matted or fixed axillary lymph nodes suggest tumor spread, as does supraclavicular or infraclavicular lymphadenopathy
claims.quote: More advanced breast cancers are characterized by 1 or more of the following examination findings: Fixation of the mass to the chest wall or to overlying skin Satellite nodules or ulcers in the skin Matted or fixed axillary lymph nodes suggest tumor spread, as does supraclavicular or infraclavicular lymphadenopathy.

claims.text: Metastatic disease may present with associated symptoms and signs (eg, pathologic fracture, abdominal pain, jaundice, dyspnea)
claims.quote: Patients with metastatic disease may present with associated symptoms and signs (eg, pathologic fracture, abdominal pain, jaundice, dyspnea).

claims.text: Treatment and next step Stages I to III: surgical removal of the tumor (breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy); radiation therapy depending on stage and surgical procedure; systemic chemotherapy may be given before surgery (neoadjuvant) and/or after (adjuvant); stage IV is treated with systemic therapy and with radiation therapy for focal disease if indicated
claims.quote: For stages I to III breast cancer, treatment involves surgical removal of the tumor (either with breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy). Radiation therapy is given depending on stage and surgical procedure. Systemic chemotherapy may be given prior to surgery (neoadjuvant) and/or postoperatively (adjuvant); indications for chemotherapy and timing depend upon the feasibility of breast-conserving surgery, patient and tumor characteristics, and presence of lymph node involvement. Stage IV is treated with systemic therapy and with radiation therapy for focal disease if indicated.

claims.text: Endocrine therapy (eg, tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor) if tumors have hormone receptors
claims.quote: Treat with endocrine therapy (eg, tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor) if tumors have hormone receptors.

claims.text: Tumors in which HER2 receptors are overexpressed are treated with medications that block these receptors
claims.quote: Tumors in which HER2 receptors are overexpressed are treated with medications that block these receptors.

claims.text: Consider treating metastatic disease to relieve symptoms (eg, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, or, for bone metastases, radiation therapy or bisphosphonates), even though survival is unlikely to be prolonged
claims.quote: Consider treating metastatic disease to relieve symptoms (eg, with chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, or, for bone metastases, radiation therapy or bisphosphonates), even though survival is unlikely to be prolonged.
